context: A screenshot of nyc-live, a 3D map of lower Manhattan rendered in a web browser and projected for an audience. A toolbar at the bottom holds the camera presets, a day/night switch and the layer toggles; place names are drawn as labels over the map.

checks.name: preset_buttons
checks.instructions: The toolbar shows five camera preset buttons labelled Venue, Battery, Brooklyn Bridge, From above and Street level.

checks.name: one_preset_active
checks.instructions: Exactly one of the camera preset buttons is highlighted as the active one, in a colour the other preset buttons do not have.

checks.name: layer_toggles_and_light
checks.instructions: The toolbar has on/off toggles for map layers (such as Buildings and Subway) and a switch between Day and Night.

checks.name: place_labels
checks.instructions: Text labels naming places, such as neighbourhoods, landmarks or the venue '598 Broadway', are drawn over the map.

checks.name: labels_apart
checks.instructions: No place label overlaps another place label.

checks.name: labels_clear_of_toolbar
checks.instructions: No place label covers the toolbar.

checks.name: stage_readability
checks.instructions: The on-screen text is readable from the back of a room: how readable is it when projected for an audience of 100 people?
